# CompressionLevelOutsideSupportedRange

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Use a supported compression level. Enabled by default; require positive semantic or local-flow proof.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
gzencode("sample",14);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Use a supported compression level.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report gzencode, gzcompress or gzdeflate level argument proven integer less than -1 or greater than 9. Skip unknown levels, default omission, and bzip2 APIs with different contracts.
- Resolve builtin functions, extension classes, method receivers, constants and named arguments. Follow unchanged locals and aliases only within the same bounded lexical scope. Require a reachable path; merge branch facts only when all incoming paths establish them.
- Emit one finding at the violating operation, not one per evidence statement. Rebinding, writes, by-reference escape and unresolved calls that can mutate relevant state remove proof. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.
- A level passed as a variable is proven only when that variable keeps its literal for the whole enclosing scope (function, method, closure or top-level code; nested function, closure and class bodies are not part of it). The same requirement applies to every variable whose value an assignment stores into it, directly or through further assignments.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Exclude shadowed builtins, unresolved receivers, incomplete syntax and unknown prerequisite facts. An extension function name alone does not prove an application function is that builtin.
- A dominating valid guard or repair described in Detection prevents the finding. Both legacy noinspection and custos-ignore forms suppress this ID.
- No report for a variable level when, anywhere in the enclosing scope and wherever it happens relative to the call, one of these reaches the variable: `++` or `--` on it or on one of its elements; a `catch`, `foreach` key or value binding it; a reference to it (a by-reference assignment on either side, a by-reference `foreach` over it, a by-reference array item, a by-reference capture by a nested closure, or an argument, other than the inspected argument itself, that a resolved callee binds by reference or that a callee custos cannot resolve receives); a write naming its target at run time (a variable variable, `extract()`, one-argument `parse_str()` or `mb_parse_str()`, `include`/`require`, `eval`); or a `$GLOBALS` access other than a literal entry naming another variable. An arrow function or a by-value import only works on a copy and keeps the proof. In top-level code a `$GLOBALS` access anywhere in the file counts too. A variable shared with other code (top-level code, `global`, `static`, a by-reference parameter, a by-reference capture by the closure that is the scope) is proven only when the scope holds no code able to run application logic: a call that is not a resolved builtin function, a method or static call, `new`, `include`/`require`, `eval`, or a closure or arrow function expression. A read inside an arrow function also checks the scopes the arrow function captures from.

## Fix

No automatic fix. The required repair depends on error handling, data selection, lifecycle ordering or application policy.

## PHP versions

Requires PHP 5.3 or later and the referenced extension API. Respect method-specific introduction versions within the supported PHP versions; unsupported optional APIs cannot establish facts. Named arguments require PHP 8.0 or later.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "CompressionLevelOutsideSupportedRange": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore CompressionLevelOutsideSupportedRange
```
